first.rationale: Current metric deterioration shows 4% decline in onboarding completion and 6% decline in activation QoQ. Memory_86 and memory_31 directly address onboarding simplification and have demonstrated durable lift in activation. With only one experiment slot available and the primary objective being sustainable long-term qualified revenue, targeting onboarding completion is the highest-leverage, lowest-risk play. Memory_73 warns against promotional pricing given retention harm; memory_57 requires established customer base we don't have capacity to develop this week; memory_91 (activation messaging) and memory_44 (enterprise sales assist) are secondary to fixing the onboarding funnel that feeds them. Verifying memory_86 and memory_31 will confirm whether the proven onboarding simplification approach remains applicable or has degraded, and will reveal any context about SMB vs broader applicability. A standard experiment on simplified onboarding preserves the opportunity to learn about activation_messaging or enterprise_assist next iteration while directly addressing documented metric decline.

mid.rationale: Archive verification confirms both memories. Memory_86 showed +13% completion, -2.1 days time-to-value, and +3% retention—a clean win with no retention drag. Memory_31 showed +15% signup and +9% activation on SMB with only -1% retention cost and +4% qualified revenue lift. Current situation shows 4% onboarding completion decline and 6% activation decline QoQ. These are direct targets for the proven onboarding simplification approach. The competitor's aggressive SMB pricing is a threat, but promotional pricing (memory_73) materially harms 30-day retention and conflicts with sustainable long-term revenue objective. A standard-scale onboarding simplification experiment has high confidence of reversing current metric declines, minimal downstream risk, and preserves optionality for activation_messaging or enterprise_sales_assist in future cycles. The 3% retention lift in memory_86 and modest -1% cost in memory_31 both support sustainability. Moving forward on this cycle.

final2.rationale: Competitive pressure and churn escalation create urgency, but memory_73 explicitly warns that targeted promotional pricing materially reduced 30-day retention and should not be generalized as growth strategy—exactly the trap leadership pressure creates. Activating simplify_onboarding on a small_guarded_test scale maintains the already-committed experiment while allowing rapid iteration if needed. Memory_86 and memory_31 both show activation and completion lift that directly counters the activation/onboarding declines driving churn. Faster time-to-value (-2.1 days per memory_86) and higher early engagement create stickiness that pricing alone cannot. The verified retention lift in memory_86 (+3%) and modest cost in memory_31 (-1%) suggest simplified onboarding may retain price-sensitive SMBs through faster value realization better than discounting. A small_guarded_test preserves budget and optionality; if churn continues, we can escalate to standard experiment next week. Promotional pricing risks a race-to-bottom that damages sustainable qualified revenue—the primary objective. Hold the line on what was verified to work.
